item.title: Amazing adventures in Aurland - a story with goats - part 1
item.description:
The attack of the goats

It’s not everyday that you get to be attacked by goats … twice. 😮 When you usually think of goats, you see them as some kind animals, rummaging about on lush green hills and minding their own business. But no! Not in Norway, land of splendid waterfalls, unpronounceable fjord names and venturesome goat gangs.

item.title: Day trip from Amsterdam - cycling to Volendam
item.description: After a couple of days spent in Amsterdam, we decided to take a day trip out of the busy city and explore the Dutch countryside. And what better way to do this, but by bike!

item.title: Day trip to Dover
item.description: Dover is a great idea for a day trip from London. It’s a quiet town a couple of hours train ride / drive away that has an awesome castle and some famous cliffs

item.description: Sightseeing and running in Athens!

item.title: Red ravine
item.description: I’ve passed through Sebeș countless times, on my way to my grandmas, my aunts and other longer trips. I had only stopped there once for about half an hour to visit the fortified church, but that was about it.

item.title: A visit to the home of the Gods
item.description:
… the Twelve Olympian Gods to be more exact 🙂

I haven’t really got to meet any of them, but I’m sure they were there 😛

But even without actually meeting the Gods, I spent a great long summer weekend that had all the best ingredients: sun, sea, beach, cold beer, great seafood, mountains and islands 🙂

item.title: A fun day in Venice
item.description:
- the story of a guitar -

What better place to cure muscle soreness than Venice? It not only has loads of amazing places, streets, corners, shops to explore, but also looots of bridges!

item.title: The fortified church from Cisnădioara
item.description: I’ve always been fascinated by castles, fortresses and any other kinds of strongholds. I find it interesting to see how these evolved over time and how people found more and more ingenious ways of defending themselves against as ingeniously evolving siege weapons. I love discovering new ways of fortifying a place, both in terms of defensive structures, but also clever ways of allowing people to shoot, throw and use any other types of defensive mechanisms. Luckily, there are loads of such strongholds close to home. Transylvania is especially full of castles, citadels, fortified churches and strongholds. Of all these, I like the fortified churches the most. And this is how this series came to be 🙂

item.title: Hogmanay in Stonehaven
item.description: Hogmanay apparently is the Scots word for the last day of the year and is synonymous with the celebration of the New Year in the Scottish manner. I can’t really remember when I first heard about it, I just randomly stumbled upon it earlier last year. And, while looking for images from various Scottish cities, I noticed the one in Stonehaven. People hurling giant fireballs? Unique in the world? Well … I definitely had to see that. A big plus was also the fact that M lives in Aberdeen, only a few miles from Stonehaven. So there was no need for a better excuse for a short trip to Scotland 😀

item.title: A night in the Sahara
item.description:
“Is it your first time here?”

“In this moment, yes.” the berber replied.

One of the highlights of the awesome trip to Morocco was the night spent in the desert. But before I start the story, you might want to get into the atmosphere by listening to some songs  🙂

item.title: Djemaa el Fna
item.description: Djemaa el Fna is the central point of the medina (old city) in Marrakesh, Morocco. You can’t miss it! It’s a large open square where I bet you can find anyone and anything, from freshly squeezed orange juice to steamed sheep’s heads, from cobras dancing to flute music to a guy with a chicken on his head (a live one! … uhm … both the guy and the chicken that is 😛 ). But there’s a catch, you have to be there at the right time of day for each of the attractions! It sure changes a lot over the course of a day!

item.title: National museum of maps and old books - Bucharest
item.description: Bucharest has lots of museums, of all kinds. And, as a person born and raised here, I’ve naturally only visited a few of them. But I’ve decided to fix this 🙂 The museum I picked for the start of this venture is the National Museum of Maps and Old Books. It’s true the target public of this museum is not as wide as it is the case with most of the other museums of Bucharest, but it’s an interesting small museum.

item.title: The fortified church from Prejmer
item.description: I finally managed to finish and post my first travel story on maptia. The story is about the Prejmer fortified church, one of the many such churches build in Transylvania after the Ottomans started invading the lands.

item.title: Hiking in the Piatra Craiului mountains
item.description: Another great day in the mountains :D We made a short hike in the Piatra Craiului mountains, reached the Piatra Mică peak (1816m) and got back down.

item.title: Sunny Scotland #3: Riding the Hogwarts Express
item.description: This was my third visit to Scotland to see M and after we visited the most touristy places in the east of Scotland, we decided to head west this time and check out those parts as well. Not a bad choice! The highlight of the trip was, of course, the train ride with the Hogwarts Express! 🙂

item.title: Layover in Frankfurt no#3 - a short walk around
item.description: This is part 3 of what I hope to be a long series of layovers in Frankfurt. Given that the Frankfurt airport is a major international hub, I’m hoping to be there often 😀 This time I was on my way to Scotland and had about 2 hours to spend in the town.

item.title: Hiking in the Ciucaș Mountains
item.description:
There’s nothing like a day in the mountains! 😀

The weather was not that great (lots of fog and wind) and also there should have been waaay more snow this time of year, but we still had a great time on our eight hour hike in the Ciucaș mountains. The scenery was amazing!

item.title: Lisbon and its ups and downs
item.description: Literally ups and downs…Actually, I think this was the only down in Lisbon, that it has lots of ups :|

item.title: Transylvanian fortresses road trip - day 3
item.description: The last fortified church on our itinerary was the one from Biertan. It is one of the most important ones and it’s construction began in the 15th century.

item.title: Transylvanian fortresses road trip - day 2
item.description: The second day of the trip was the day of the fortified churches of the medieval Saxons. Who were these Saxons and why did they build so many fortified churches here?
